## Natural history notes

A tiny delphacid planthopper characterized by a narrow wedge-shaped body, short hopping legs, and delicate wings that may be held roof-like over the body. In Florida, Bostaera balli is recorded from the state and belongs to a grass- and sedge-associated group of planthoppers, so it is most likely encountered in moist grassy habitats, marsh edges, wet prairies, ditches, or other low vegetation where host plants occur. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap, while also serving as prey for spiders, predatory bugs, small wasps, and other insect predators.
